Trump said last week that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, while Moscow partially lifted its ban on diesel exports from Oct. 10 following the agreement. "The diesel has started reaching global markets and is expected to have a positive effect on stabilising oil markets, although it will not be enough to fully stabilize them," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a daily conference call. LSEG data showed on Wednesday that Russia had resumed diesel export loadings from the Baltic port of Primorsk. According to the shipping data, a tanker carrying around 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel was loaded on Tuesday and was heading towards Morocco. opinion Trump’s Russian Diesel Debacle Risks Backfiring Read more Under the terms announced by Trump last Friday, Russia agreed to immediately release more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel onto global marke

title: Moscow Court Places Prominent Economist Under House Arrest in Bribery Case
text: Moscow Court Places Prominent Economist Under House Arrest in Bribery Case Oct. 15, 2026 Sergei Sinelnikov-Murylev. Andrei Lyubimov / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has placed prominent establishment economist Sergei Sinelnikov-Murylev under house arrest on bribery charges, the RBC news outlet reported Thursday, citing law enforcement sources. Sinelnikov-Murylev, 66, is a senior researcher at the Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy and the former president of the Economic Development Ministry’s Russian Academy of Foreign Trade. He received state awards and a presidential commendation in 2018 for contributing to Russia’s 2018-24 national development strategy. He also joined the government’s expert council in December 2022. The Zamoskvoretsky District Court reportedly granted the investigation’s request to place Sinelnikov-Murylev under house arrest for two months. The 66-year-old economist faces up to 15 years in prison if found guilty of receiving a large-scale bribe. Specific details on the alleged bribe amount or the involved parties have not been disclosed . The Interfax news agency reported that the case material is available on the court’s website. text: FSB Arrests Swede in Pskov Region Over Border Crossing and Sabotage Allegations Oct. 15, 2026 FSB Russia’s FSB security service said Thursday it has arrested a Swedish citizen in the northwestern Pskov region on allegations of illegally crossing the border to carry out sabotage attacks against military facilities. An FSB video published by the state-run news agency TASS showed the man identifying himself through an interpreter as 35-year-old Freddy Michael Stålkrantz Lindholm. In a statement on its website, the FSB said it had detained Lindholm in the Sebezhsky district near the border with Latvia and Belarus. It did not indicate from which country he crossed into Russia. The FSB claimed he crossed into Russian territory under the guise of enlisting in the Russian military, with the alleged intent of committing “sabotage and terrorist acts at military facilities.” The FSB said Lindholm served as a contracted service member in Ukraine from February to June this year as a squad commander operating drones. text: Ukraine residents 'too exhausted' for sirens Image source, Gregory Ebbs Image caption, Gregory Ebbs (left) took a donated Citroen Xsara to Ukraine, filled with aid By Clare Ashford BBC Radio Shropshire Published 7 hours ago A councillor who delivered aid to Ukraine has said people there are "exhausted" and no longer wake up for air raid sirens because of their frequency. Gregory Ebbs, Liberal Democrat councillor for Whitchurch South in Shropshire, travelled to Lviv and Kyiv to deliver a donated a car along with medical supplies, tools and warm clothing. The former Apprentice contestant said local people told him they no longer go to bomb shelters unless there is a ballistic missile alert. "There's a certain degree of exhaustion," he told the BBC. "People are surprised - they ask why you're there - they love that fact that volunteers go out there... but they're just exhausted". First heading to the western city of Lviv, Ebbs said they delivered the aid to humanitarian organisation, the PTAHA. text: Уряд ухвалив рішення щодо організації навчання під час тривалих повітряних тривог. Громади мають приділити особливу увагу цьому завданню та допомогти закладам освіти адаптувати освітній процес до безпекових викликів. Зокрема, опрацювати можливість використання інших облаштованих укриттів для проведення навчання. Кожна школа самостійно визначає модель навчання з урахуванням безпекової ситуації, місткості та облаштування укриття. Заняття можуть відбуватися в класах, укриттях або поєднувати очний і дистанційний формати. Батьки мають заздалегідь знати, як проходитиме навчання, мати можливість планувати свій день, тому розклади повинні бути гнучкими, а формати навчання — прогнозованими. Якщо укриття не дозволяє очно провести всі заняття, пріоритет надається предметам математичної, природничої, мовно-літературної, громадянської та історичної освітніх галузей. Інші предмети за потреби можна вивчати дистанційно. Укриття шкіл, які працюють очно, повинні бути придатними для тривалого перебування дітей. Maduro, shackled at the ankles, was brought to court to face the new charges accusing the couple of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans. text: Senators celebrate the approval of a constitutional amendment bill that would end shorten the workweek in Brazil. In an attempt to overturn the first-round lead secured by his opponent, far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which will give some workers an extra day off each week. title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region

title: EU must curb energy prices to prevent people turning to populists, commissioner warns – as it happened
text: 10.03 EDT EU has to act on energy prices to prevent people from turning to populists and extremists, EU commissioner warns Jennifer Rankin in Brussels Europe has to take action to curb soaring oil and gas prices to prevent people from turning to populists and extremists, a senior EU official has said. European Commissioner for Energy Dan Jørgensen Photograph: Omar Havana/Reuters Dan Jørgensen, the European commissioner for energy and housing policy, said EU governments could choose actions to make fossil fuels cheaper as long as they were “targeted” and “temporary” so as not to derail the continent from its goal to tackle the climate crisis by drastically cutting carbon emissions. Earlier this week European gas prices hit their highest level since the winter of 2022, when consumers faced rising prices in the wake of supply disruption following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine . title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes as Trump ‘energy ceasefire’ collapses

Moscow accused Ukraine of launching a strike against a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region, its first since Trump abruptly declared an “energy ceasefire” that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to. title: Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 34 children and teacher
text: A total of 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the roof caved in. Photograph: Reuters View image in fullscreen A total of 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the roof caved in. Photograph: Reuters Pakistan Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 34 children and teacher Another three pupils from al-Khair school in Peshawar in critical condition after search for survivors Reuters in Islamabad Thu 15 Oct 2026 04.25 EDT Last modified on Thu 15 Oct 2026 14.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher have died after the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city ⁠of Peshawar. As panicked parents ​and relatives thronged the site of the privately run al-Khair school to search for their loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble. Most of the victims were under 13 years old ⁠and from low-income households. At least 45 children suffered injuries, ranging from minor wounds to severe trauma, said Arif Khattak, the regional director of emergency services. title: Will Trump’s economy sink Republicans in the US midterm elections? Our reporters answered your questions
text: The high cost of living has Americans angrier than ever. Guardian reporters answered your questions about the US economy ahead of November Sign up for the Stakes newsletter for more midterms coverage Send us your questions on Trump’s immigration agenda ahead of the midterms LucccA asks: Why are labor unions in the US still not as well-organized compared to the rest of the world? I know there was a push against them in the past—does that still have an effect today? Also, why are there so many right-leaning unions in the US? Michael: A lot of reasons. The US has low union density compared to other wealthy nations, currently at 10.0%, and that has been on a precipitous decline for the past few decades for a variety of reasons that include anti-union and union busting campaigns, outdated labor laws where employers often retaliate for union organizing or delay bargaining for years, as we are seeing with Starbucks, where there is no union contract after nearly five years since the first store won its union election in December 2021.Right to work laws in the US also undermine labor unions and starve them of resources.
